obligation: Title IV breach report to FSA
citation: SAIG Enrollment Agreement (per DCL GEN-15-18); FSA Cybersecurity Breach Intake
deadline: Immediately upon an actual or suspected breach
notify: FSA (CPSSAIG@ed.gov and/or the FSA Cybersecurity Breach Intake Form)

deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC (online form), when unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers is acquired without authorization

obligation: State data breach notification (Florida worked example); state student-data laws
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(3)-(5). Each other state where affected residents live applies its own statute (not reviewed here). State student-privacy laws can add duties (not reviewed here)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: Individuals: as expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred (15 more days if good cause is given in writing to the department within 30 days). Department of Legal Affairs: no later than 30 days, if 500 or more Floridians. Consumer reporting agencies: without unreasonable delay, if more than 1,000 individuals
notify: Affected Florida residents; Florida Department of Legal Affairs (500 or more); nationwide consumer reporting agencies (more than 1,000). State education agency duties under student-data laws not reviewed

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident / ransom payment report (proposed) - NOT YET IN EFFECT; final rule pending
deadline: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered incident occurred; 24 hours after a ransom payment
